title: Unearned Hazard Premium on a Withdrawn Reserve-Paid Term: Flat and Short-Rate Cancellations
content:
Q&A for the servicing desk on the unearned hazard premium of a withdrawn hazard insurance term that a Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve under Set-Aside Accounts paid.

**When is the whole payment unearned?**
Where the days in force — the calendar days from the day the withdrawn term began to the cancellation date — are zero, the flat basis applies: the whole payment is unearned, because the term was cancelled before it began.

**When does the short-rate basis apply?**
Where the days in force are above zero and the cancellation date is the due date of a paid replacement hazard bill — the latest paid hazard insurance bill falls due on or after the day the withdrawn term began, and its due date is the cancellation date — the short-rate basis applies, because the borrower's side asked for the cancellation. The unearned hazard premium is then the reserve's payment of the withdrawn term times the whole months left after the month in which the cancellation falls, divided by twelve. Those months left are twelve less the months in force less one, never below zero; the months in force are the whole calendar months from the day the term began to the cancellation date.

**What if neither applies?**
Where the days in force are above zero and the cancellation date is not a paid replacement bill's due date, this rule does not set the unearned premium.

## Short-rate figures on a hypothetical payment of 1,200.00

| Months in force | Months left (twelve less months in force less one) | Unearned premium |
|---|---|---|
| 0 (days in force above zero) | 11 | 1,100.00 |
| 3 | 8 | 800.00 |
| 10 | 1 | 100.00 |
| 11 | 0 | 0.00 |

With zero days in force the same payment is unearned in full, 1,200.00.
